messages.content: I want to get some rest

function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food from selected restaurants with specified items and their quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurants.description: The name of the restaurant from which the user wants to order food. Use the exact name as registered on Uber Eats.

items.description: A list of item names that the user wants to order from the restaurant.

quantities.description: A list of integers, each representing the quantity of the corresponding item in the order. The quantities should align with the items list by index.

message.content: Sounds like a good idea—sometimes a short break is all you need. If you’d like to order something to keep you company while you rest, just let me know what you’re craving!
message.reasoning: The user says "I want to get some rest". This is not a request to place an order. We need to respond appropriately. The user might want to rest, maybe they want to order food? But the user didn't specify. We can ask clarifying question: "Would you like to order food or something else?" Or we can respond with a supportive message: "Sure, take a break." But we might also ask if they want to order food. The user didn't mention ordering. So we should respond politely. There's no function call needed.
